pr_title: Ensure HttpData#addContent/setContent releases the buffer before throwing IOException
pr_body:
Motivation:
When the `ByteBuf` size exceeds the max limit/defined size, `IOException` is thrown.
`HttpData#addContent/setContent` should release the buffer in such cases otherwise memory leak will happen.

Modification:
- Release the provided `ByteBuf` before throwing `IOException`
- Add unit tests

Result:
Fixes #11618

> Hmm.. let me think about if the caller should release it or not. @chrisvest @NiteshKant @ejona86 WDYT ?

Yeah I also was thinking about that, but it is something like a mix :(
For example in 

https://github.com/netty/netty/blob/6a7cccded07a46a0a7b50ac27ff3f86eb977859f/codec-http/src/main/java/io/netty/handler/codec/http/multipart/AbstractDiskHttpData.java#L187

https://github.com/netty/netty/blob/6a7cccded07a46a0a7b50ac27ff3f86eb977859f/codec-http/src/main/java/io/netty/handler/codec/http/multipart/AbstractDiskHttpData.java#L147

the buffer is released in try/finally

and here the buffer is released if empty

https://github.com/netty/netty/blob/6a7cccded07a46a0a7b50ac27ff3f86eb977859f/codec-http/src/main/java/io/netty/handler/codec/http/multipart/AbstractMemoryHttpData.java#L112

I _think_ the HttpData object is supposed to own the buffer, and therefor also has responsibility to release. An exception at the point of transfer is a bit of a grey area, but I think it's a safer default to have the HttpData release in that case. This detail should be documented in the HttpData.setContent javadoc. Then, if a caller knows how to handle this exception, they can do a reference count dance around the call to setContent.

It seems like the expectation from `[add, set]Content` is that they take ownership of the passed `ByteBuf`, so sounds reasonable to make sure it is released if we won't be using it in the error cases.

So I was thinking a bit more about this... Imho we should not release before we throw but the caller should release in case of an exception. This is inline with what we do in other places like `CompositeByteBuf`.

> So I was thinking a bit more about this... Imho we should not release before we throw but the caller should release in case of an exception. This is inline with what we do in other places like `CompositeByteBuf`.

What should we do in these cases where the buffer is released in try/finally - keep them as they are at the moment?

@normanmaurer so I casually scanned for usages of `CompositeByteBuf#addComponent()` and the first usage I looked at was [DeflateDecoder](https://github.com/netty/netty/blob/4.1/codec-http/src/main/java/io/netty/handler/codec/http/websocketx/extensions/compression/DeflateDecoder.java#L134) and it does not handle the case if `addComponent()` throws hence leaking the buffer. I think ensuring the methods that take a `ByteBuf` takes ownership is a much safer approach than making sure the buffer is released if the method throws but not when it succeeds.
